**Coordinated abuse is a pattern across entities and time, not just suspicious wording.** Several accounts may review the same businesses in synchronized bursts with reused text. Each individual review could appear ordinary, while the combined behavior reveals coordination. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.02907) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084)

Construct a time-aware graph connecting accounts, reviewed entities, and legitimately available shared signals. Combine text similarity with repeated interaction patterns, timing, and graph motifs. Use adjudicated cases and evaluate on later periods and unseen entities to avoid memorizing known rings.

**Shared behavior is evidence to investigate, not proof of abuse.** A family, workplace, or genuine fan community can share networks and interests. Test false positives on those groups and avoid allowing one weak association to contaminate an entire connected component.

Produce a risk score with inspectable evidence for reviewers, and measure precision at actual review capacity plus time-to-detection. Track appeals and corrected labels. Monitor adaptation by abusers and changing legitimate behavior. Text-only models miss coordination; graph-only systems can mistake ordinary community structure for malicious activity, so both evidence and review design matter.

**Technical details and references.**

Build a temporal heterogeneous graph of accounts, reviewed entities, devices/network signals where legitimately available, and shared content. Combine text similarity with synchronized activity, repeated reviewer–business patterns, and abnormal graph motifs. Train on adjudicated cases with temporal/entity-separated validation. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.02907) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084)

Coordinated legitimate behavior can resemble a ring, so output risk scores and evidence for review rather than automatically treating graph proximity as guilt. Use robust negative sampling, monitor adversarial adaptation, and limit sensitive features to authorized purposes. Evaluate precision at reviewer capacity, false positives on new/shared-network users, and time-to-detection. Preserve provenance and an appeal/review path. Text-only classifiers miss coordination; graph-only classifiers can overflag communities with normal shared interests.
